quotes: Call 999 if:
you get sudden pain or discomfort in your chest that does not go away – the pain can feel like squeezing or pressure inside your chest, burning or indigestion
you get pain that spreads to your left or right arm, or your neck, jaw, stomach or back
you have chest pain and you feel sweaty, sick, light headed or short of breath
You could be having a heart attack. Call 999 straight away as you need immediate treatment in hospital.
Most chest pain is not a sign of anything serious but get medical advice just in case.

quotes: Call 999 or go to A&E immediately if:
you have severe difficulty breathing – you’re gasping, choking or not able to get words out
your chest feels tight or heavy
you have pain that spreads to your arms, back, neck and jaw
your lips or skin are turning very pale, blue or grey
you feel suddenly confused
Contact NHS 111 if:
you have difficulty breathing – you may be more short of breath than usual

quotes: See a GP if:
you have fainted
Call 999 if someone:
cannot be woken up within 1 minute
has not fully recovered or has difficulty with speech or movement
has chest pain or a pounding, fluttering or irregular heartbeat (heart palpitations)
is shaking or jerking (having a seizure or fit)

quotes: Call 999 and ask for an ambulance if:
it's the first time someone has had a seizure
the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if you do not know how long their seizures usually last
the person does not regain full consciousness, or has several seizures without regaining consciousness
People with epilepsy do not always need an ambulance or to go to hospital every time they have a seizure.

quotes: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
You or your child are vomiting blood (or have vomited blood) and:
feel confused
feel faint or dizzy
have rapid or shallow breathing
have cold, clammy, pale skin
have black poo
If you have stopped vomiting blood and had no other symptoms, ask for an urgent GP appointment, call 111 or get help from 111 online.

you're coughing up blood and finding it hard to breathe, have a very fast heartbeat or have pain in your chest or upper back

quotes: Call 999 if:
your lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly become swollen
you're breathing very fast or struggling to breathe (you may become very wheezy or feel like you're choking or gasping for air)
your throat feels tight or you're struggling to swallow
you suddenly become very confused, drowsy or dizzy
someone faints and cannot be woken up
These can be signs of a serious allergic reaction and may need immediate treatment in hospital.

quotes: If you're feeling like you want to end your life, it's important to tell someone.
Help and support is available right now if you need it. You do not have to struggle with difficult feelings alone.
If you have seriously harmed yourself – for example, by taking a drug overdose – or you feel that you may be about to harm yourself, call 999 for an ambulance or go straight to A&E.

rules.title: Chest pain with signs of a heart attack

action.text: Chest pain that feels like pressure or tightness, or chest pain together with breathlessness, sweating, feeling sick or light-headed, or pain in an arm, the neck or the jaw, can be a sign of a heart attack. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice is to call an ambulance straight away for exactly these combinations.

rules.title: Severe breathing difficulty

action.text: A feeling of choking or suffocating, blue lips or skin, or breathing difficulty together with a tight or heavy chest, very pale skin, sudden confusion or pain in an arm, the neck or the jaw, needs immediate treatment. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as reasons to call an ambulance. The vocabulary has no feature for how severe the breathlessness is, so breathlessness alone is placed one level lower (see the rule on breathing difficulty).

rules.title: Signs of a stroke

action.text: Weakness or drooping on one side of the face, weakness in an arm or a leg, or slurred or difficult speech can be signs of a stroke, even if they have now stopped. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice is to call an ambulance for any of these signs, also when they have stopped. The vocabulary cannot say whether a weakness is new, so any report of one of these signs escalates.

rules.title: Seizure (fit)

action.text: A seizure (fit) needs emergency help when it is a first seizure, lasts more than 5 minutes, repeats, or the person does not fully recover. If you are not sure, treat it as an emergency. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice is an ambulance for a first seizure. The vocabulary cannot say whether a seizure is the first one, so every reported seizure escalates. People with known epilepsy do not always need an ambulance.

rules.title: Loss of consciousness with other warning signs

action.text: Losing consciousness together with chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, a seizure, difficulty with speech or movement, or breathing difficulty needs immediate help. So does anyone who cannot be woken. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as reasons to call an ambulance after a faint.

rules.title: Bleeding that is heavy or will not stop

action.text: Bleeding that is heavy or that you cannot stop needs immediate treatment. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as a reason to call an ambulance or go to an emergency department.

rules.title: Vomiting blood with other warning signs

action.text: Vomiting blood together with feeling faint, dizzy or confused, fast breathing, cold clammy skin or black stools needs immediate treatment. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as reasons to call an ambulance when someone is vomiting blood.

rules.title: Coughing up blood with other warning signs

action.text: Coughing up blood together with difficulty breathing, a very fast heartbeat or chest pain needs immediate treatment. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as reasons to call an ambulance when someone is coughing up blood.

rules.title: Signs of a severe allergic reaction

action.text: Swelling of the lips or throat, or an allergic reaction together with difficulty breathing or swallowing, confusion, dizziness or fainting, can be a severe allergic reaction. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as reasons to call an ambulance. The vocabulary cannot say whether a swelling is sudden, so any reported swelling of the lips or throat escalates.

rules.title: Thoughts of suicide or self-harm

action.text: You do not have to face this alone, and help is available right now. If you have harmed yourself or feel you may be about to, call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department, or ask someone to take you. You can also speak to a trained counsellor free of charge at any time on Tele MANAS: call 14416.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice is to tell someone and, where there is harm or a risk of it, to call an ambulance. The highest level is used so that this text is shown before anything else.

rules.title: Stiff neck or headache with signs of a serious infection

action.text: A stiff neck with a dislike of bright lights, or a headache together with a stiff neck, a dislike of bright lights, a very high temperature or confusion, can be signs of a serious infection. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as reasons to call an ambulance or go to an emergency department.

rules.title: Bleeding in pregnancy with fainting or dizziness

action.text: Bleeding in pregnancy together with feeling faint or dizzy, or losing consciousness, needs immediate treatment. Call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department. Do not drive yourself: ask someone to take you or ask for an ambulance. This is not a diagnosis.

rules.why_this_level: Published as a reason to call an ambulance. Pregnancy is outside what the product assesses, but an escalation is still shown.

rules.title: Chest pain or chest tightness

action.text: Chest pain should be checked by a doctor even when it is probably nothing serious. Please see a doctor today. Call 112 at once if the pain does not go away, feels like pressure or tightness, spreads to an arm, the neck or the jaw, or comes with breathlessness, sweating or feeling sick.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice for chest pain without the heart-attack signs is to see a doctor, not an ambulance. The draft asks for the same day and names the signs that need 112.

rules.title: Breathing difficulty

action.text: Difficulty breathing, or being more short of breath than usual, should be checked today. Please see a doctor today. Call 112 at once if you are gasping, cannot get words out, your chest feels tight or heavy, your lips or skin turn blue or very pale, or you feel suddenly confused.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice for breathing difficulty without the severe signs is urgent advice the same day.

rules.title: Fainting or loss of consciousness

action.text: Fainting or losing consciousness should be checked by a doctor to find out what caused it. Please see a doctor today. Call 112 at once if it comes with chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, a seizure, or difficulty with speech or movement, or if you have not fully recovered.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice after a simple faint is to see a doctor. The draft asks for the same day.

rules.title: Vomiting blood

action.text: Vomiting blood needs to be assessed urgently, even if it has stopped. Please see a doctor today. Call 112 at once if you feel faint, dizzy, confused or generally unwell, or have black stools.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice when the vomiting has stopped and there are no other symptoms is an urgent appointment.

rules.title: Coughing up blood

action.text: Coughing up blood, even a small amount, should be checked urgently. Please see a doctor today. Call 112 at once if it is more than a few spots or streaks, or if you also find it hard to breathe, have a very fast heartbeat or have chest pain.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice for a few spots or streaks of blood is an urgent appointment.

rules.title: Black stools, bloody diarrhoea or bleeding in the gut

action.text: Black or dark red stools, or bloody diarrhoea, should be checked urgently. Please see a doctor today. Call 112 at once if you are bleeding non-stop or there is a lot of blood.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice for black or dark red stools and for bloody diarrhoea is an urgent appointment.

rules.title: Confusion

action.text: New confusion should be checked by a doctor. Please see a doctor today. If the confusion came on suddenly, call 112 now or go to the nearest hospital emergency department.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice is an ambulance for sudden confusion and a doctor for gradual confusion. The vocabulary cannot say which it is, so the draft asks for the same day and names the sudden case.

rules.title: Bleeding or spotting in pregnancy

action.text: Bleeding or spotting in pregnancy should be checked urgently. Please contact your doctor or maternity hospital today. Call 112 at once if the bleeding is heavy, or if you have severe tummy pain, shoulder pain, or feel faint or dizzy.

rules.why_this_level: The published advice for light bleeding in pregnancy is urgent help the same day.

not_covered.sign: How severe or how sudden a symptom is (severe pain, sudden headache, sudden swelling)
not_covered.why: the feature vocabulary records that a symptom is present, not its severity or onset

not_covered.sign: Choking on food or an object, serious injury, burns, poisoning or overdose
A rash that does not fade when pressed; the other signs of sepsis
Weakness or numbness down one side of the body; sudden loss of vision
not_covered.why: the vocabulary has only general weakness, numbness and vision features, which are common without a stroke

not_covered.sign: Labour and childbirth; warning signs in babies and children
not_covered.why: outside what the product assesses (adults; no pregnancy flows)

not_covered.sign: Blood in the stool that is not black, dark red or with diarrhoea
not_covered.why: the published advice is a routine appointment, not an urgent one

open_points: The warning signs are taken from the NHS website (England). No Indian clinical source was used. A doctor practising in India should review the rules before they are approved.

The numbers 112 and 14416 could not be read on the central government's own pages (112.gov.in, mha.gov.in, telemanas.mohfw.gov.in, pib.gov.in refused automated reading). They are taken from a Kerala Police page, a Government of Assam hospital page and a JIPMER page. The owner should open the official pages and confirm both numbers before approval.
The ambulance number 108 is not used: no official page stating it could be read, and it differs between states.
Each urgency level is the assistant's choice within the published advice. Where the vocabulary cannot tell a severe or sudden case from a mild one, the draft escalates.
The rules have not been tried on real cases. No urgency labels exist to measure how often they would fire wrongly or miss.
